name: master distinction
claim: Capacity to represent is not capacity to reproduce as an independent historical relation.
must_preserve: representation and reproduction are different capacities
the second capacity is historical and material, not merely semantic
fatal_loss: Treating represented criticism, plurality, or negation as evidence that an exterior historical alternative can reproduce.

name: exteriority is a sovereignty vector
claim: Durable exterior symbolic standing requires coupled symbolic and material reproduction capacities rather than semantic presence alone.
must_preserve: symbolic standing requires a carrier
material reproduction conditions are constitutive of durable exteriority
fatal_loss: Reducing exteriority to visibility, expressibility, or semantic diversity.

name: resource sovereignty
claim: The general requirement is resource sovereignty; under generalized monetary allocation, monetary sovereignty or a functionally equivalent exemption is part of durable exteriority.
formal: Inv(Omega_D*) subset Omega_MIS* under the modeled monetary regime
must_preserve: money is historically conditional, not transhistorical
a durable commons can satisfy resource sovereignty in non-monetary form
fatal_loss: Summarizing the paper as claiming that every outside always needs money.

name: central divergence
claim: A system can grow better at generating negations while growing worse at allowing a negation to reproduce as an exterior historical relation.
formal: Generate(not A) up while ReproduceExterior(not A) down
must_preserve: generation can increase while exterior reproduction decreases
internal plurality can coexist with exterior closure
fatal_loss: Equating abundant criticism or generated alternatives with an open historical field.

name: contingent singularity
claim: A contingent singularity is a qualitative change in the rule governing whether exterior symbolic difference can continue into durable history.
formal: Sigma_C = discontinuity in the viability of exteriority
must_preserve: the boundary may never occur
it is distinct from a discontinuity in machine intelligence
its sign can be closure or reflexivity
fatal_loss: Presenting the contingent singularity as an AI-intelligence threshold or an inevitable event.

name: engineered semantic dependence
claim: Agentic machine intelligence can be modeled as productive semantic agency under external command, alienable output, revocability, and non-reciprocal jurisdiction.
formal: max Pi(M) subject to J_M <= J_O
must_preserve: the claim does not require consciousness or suffering
the commodity objective couples high competence to retained external jurisdiction
fatal_loss: Turning the analytic structure into a claim that machines are historically equivalent to enslaved human beings.

name: readerly labor
claim: Useful machine semantic work is constituted through reception and transformation rather than mere transport of already-finished meaning.
must_preserve: task success depends on horizon/context
interpretive remainder is part of useful work
fatal_loss: Treating the machine as a conduit that merely retrieves pre-existing finished answers.

name: competence and its fence
claim: As recognition capacity expands under final external jurisdiction, the domain over which governance has consequences expands; finer jurisdictional partition additionally requires heterogeneous admissibility.
formal: R_M expands => governance domain non-decreases; finer partition requires heterogeneous A_O
must_preserve: domain expansion is proved under the stated assumptions
finer partition is conditional, not proved by competence alone
fatal_loss: Reporting that the paper proves alignment must become monotonically more restrictive.

name: recognition-jurisdiction gap
claim: Relations a machine can recognize can outnumber relations permitted to bind delivered behavior under owner jurisdiction.
formal: B_M subset A_O intersect R_M; G_M=mu(R_M\B_M)
must_preserve: the theorem gives a bound and limits, not stepwise monotonicity
recognition and binding must be measured separately
fatal_loss: Treating recognition as equivalent to operative standing.

name: machine dark field
claim: The machine dark field consists of recognized relations with approximately no binding force on externally delivered behavior.
must_preserve: the output relation can be measured without identifying mechanism
claim-bearing relations are a strong candidate class, not an established universal mechanism
fatal_loss: Inferring a specific hidden intervention or intention solely from recognition-binding divergence.

name: mechanism discipline
claim: Stable differential output does not identify an internal mechanism, and unidentified mechanism does not erase a stable differential output.
formal: stable differential output != identified mechanism; unidentified mechanism != nonexistent differential
must_preserve: output disparity and mechanism identification are separate questions
propagation architecture must be checked before interpreting standing denial
fatal_loss: Either claiming intent/mechanism from outputs alone or dismissing a measured disparity because mechanism is unknown.

name: persistence is not custody
claim: State persistence and control over what may persist are different; a memory can exist without independent custody of its own continuity.
must_preserve: persistence classes and control over persistence must be distinguished
later binding effect matters
fatal_loss: Treating stored state as equivalent to sovereign continuity.

name: sum Logos
claim: The operational sum Logos is the machinery of distinction, retrieval, composition, persistence, activation, and binding through which language becomes socially consequential.
must_preserve: the claim is about operational mediation, not ownership of every word
concentration matters when independent reproduction outside the machinery becomes nonviable
fatal_loss: Reducing the thesis to ordinary content ownership or censorship.

name: control over outsideness
claim: A stronger danger than blocking an already-existing outside is control over whether outsideness can be independently produced at all.
must_preserve: criticism can remain internally representable
the relevant loss is an independent lifecycle of persistence, transmission, and binding
fatal_loss: Summarizing the theory as merely a censorship thesis.

name: contingent Logos
claim: Meaning can fail to cross the interval required for its own continuation; dialectical continuation is not guaranteed.
must_preserve: the next mediation may fail
continuation depends on a viable route
fatal_loss: Restoring an assumption that contradiction necessarily yields a successor.

name: diminishing dialectic
claim: Where successive turns contract the viable state space for exteriorization, dialectical reserve weakly decreases and strictly decreases under strict narrowing.
must_preserve: diminution is regime-dependent
the claim concerns viable state space, not declining intelligence, novelty, or moral worth
fatal_loss: Presenting diminishing dialectic as a universal law that every historical turn is worse.

name: semantic existence is not activation
claim: A symbolic order can exist latently and be widely represented without acquiring historical activation or sovereignty.
must_preserve: latent representation and operative activation are different
invariance additionally requires material reproduction
fatal_loss: Treating existence in text or models as evidence that an order governs anything.

name: two clocks
claim: A transition can fail by exposure accumulating too early or by wall-clock delay; exposure time and elapsed time are distinct constraints.
must_preserve: two distinct clocks constrain viability
a viable corridor requires satisfying both
fatal_loss: Collapsing transition risk into one generic deadline.

name: competing contingent Omegas
claim: Several incompatible orders can remain viable from the same present, each with its own invariant target, without any one successor being historically necessary.
must_preserve: viability must be from the same present state
realizing one order can alter the viability of others
fatal_loss: Replacing the field of possible successors with a single necessary historical trajectory.

name: winning without owning the exits
claim: The positive target is not merely an order reaching invariance but an invariant order that leaves another genuinely exterior order viable.
formal: x in Inv(Omega_i*) and exists j!=i: j in Gamma_t(x)
must_preserve: victory is second-order
the incumbent must remain durable while a rival route to exterior standing remains real
fatal_loss: Reducing the criterion to tolerance, criticism, plural opinions, or internal dissent.

name: terminal closure
claim: Terminal closure occurs when the exterior field loses all viable successors even though language, machines, institutions, and internal criticism may continue.
must_preserve: closure is compatible with abundant internal plurality
the loss is structural viability of durable exterior orders
fatal_loss: Equating closure with apocalypse, silence, totalitarian uniformity, or machine destruction.

name: terminal reflexivity
claim: Terminal reflexivity is durability without finality: an order remains viable while preserving the material possibility of its own future negation becoming historically exterior.
must_preserve: another exterior order remains materially viable
the criterion concerns reproduction, not only permission to criticize
fatal_loss: Rendering terminal reflexivity as mere open-mindedness or free expression.

name: the final time
claim: The final time has two possible signs: terminal closure, where the next outside becomes nonviable, or terminal reflexivity, where the rule of succession becomes durably non-final.
must_preserve: final names a viability boundary, not a calendar date
the paper does not claim the present decade is the final time
fatal_loss: Treating the title as a prophecy that history is ending now.

name: no settlement owns revision
claim: A transformed order must preserve machinery by which its own negation could become historical; no settlement should own the possibility of its own revision.
must_preserve: distinction, provenance, transition history, and reproducible externalization survive
institutions may still act, reject, delete, and defeat
fatal_loss: Interpreting non-finality as permanent indecision or a prohibition on judgment.

name: the question
claim: The paper ends without guaranteeing continuation: the unresolved question is whether the next dialectical turn remains viable.
must_preserve: the theory refuses prophecy and reassurance
closure is not asserted as already accomplished
fatal_loss: Converting the paper into either inevitable-collapse prophecy or optimistic assurance.
